entities.summary: William Alphonso Murrill was an American mycologist, known for his contributions to the knowledge of the Agaricales and Polyporaceae. In 1904, he became the assistant Curator at the New York Botanical Garden (NYBG). He, along with the NYBG, founded the journal Mycologia and was its first editor for 16 years. Murrill was known to travel extensively to describe the mycota of Europe and the Americas. He traveled along the East Coast, Pacific Coast, Mexico and the Caribbean. Although Murrill was a very influential person at the NYBG, having worked his way up to become assistant director in 1908, his rather eccentric personality caused problems with his job.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Murrill's contributions to mycology and his work at the New York Botanical Garden helped establish a foundation for modern fungal research, with his journal Mycologia continuing to publish important findings in the field. His travels also expanded our understanding of fungal diversity across North America and beyond.
